standard_prerequisites.name: The generic structure
standard_prerequisites.statement: The generic is the model obtained by the amalgamation construction from the finite unconfined systems, with a distinguished set of vertices.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the structure shown to be free.

standard_prerequisites.name: Freely generated system
standard_prerequisites.statement: A system is freely generated by a set when that set is independent and the system is generated by it.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the conclusion of the statement.

standard_prerequisites.name: Extension of finite embeddings
standard_prerequisites.statement: Finiteness of the generating data makes every partial embedding from a finite subset extend to an embedding of the generated subsystem.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is what forces the universal mapping property.

core_obligations: First show that the generic is a Steiner triple system, by adjoining a new vertex to two distinct elements to form a block and using the genericity to embed the resulting finite system (source line 762).

Then show that the generic is freely generated by a countable set: the independence follows because every finite partial map extends over the generated subsystem, which is finite, and the generating condition follows from the construction of the generic (source lines 762-764).

proof_roadmap.step: Show the product of two distinct elements exists.
Show independence and generation, hence freeness.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled proposition at source lines 760-761: the generic structure is isomorphic to the free Steiner triple system on countably many generators. The proof (source lines 762-765) does two things that the statement hides: it first checks that the generic really is a Steiner triple system, by adjoining a new vertex to two distinct elements and invoking genericity to embed the resulting finite configuration, and then obtains freeness by verifying independence (every partial map from a finite subset extends, because the subsystem generated by a finite set is finite, so the extension criterion applies) together with the generating condition. The statement records only the isomorphism.
